spine: Hem, sleepless in a shut carriage, realises that morning will bring shame to her home.
fidelity: Reviewed against scenes 13-15: the carriage stays shut (slats, no open window) and is moving away fast ('দ্রুতবেগে') by this paragraph; Calcutta is flat (no hills or towers); night ambience only on night pictures, morning crows/birds on the morning pictures 9-10; Hem is a 14-year-old widow in plain white, shown only in close-up, with no mole (owner decision 27 Nov 2026); the daughters of good families wear coloured, bordered saris, never widow's white; the morning material is Hem's imagined future, bracketed by her face; scene 15's first shot must be Hem's present close-up, closing the bracket of shots 9-12 across the scene boundary; the mother is the same veiled woman throughout (white sari, red border, head covered); neighbours: women in front, men at the gate; period-correct, nothing modern. Owner waiver 27 Nov 2026: the 4 s shot minimum (spec section 8) is waived for shots 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 (first for 5, 6 and 7; extended to 2 (2.84 s), 3 (3.95 s) and 8 (3.77 s) by the owner on 27 Nov 2026).

shots.subject: an empty narrow North Calcutta lane at deep night, moonlit, no vehicle, no people, no animals: wheel ruts in the dust lead away between two rows of shut houses (the shut houses carry 'পৃথিবীতে ঘরে ঘরে'); the lane runs to a flat Calcutta horizon under the moon; the hooves and wheels fade away on the soundtrack, as if Hem's carriage has just turned out of sight (new still, stills-f01s014-fix-r3)
